q: Centre manifold reduction is used in bifurcation theory to:
opts: Eliminate all hyperbolic (stable/unstable) directions and reduce the dynamics to the low-dimensional centre manifold
exp: Near a bifurcation, the centre manifold carries the interesting dynamics. Stable/unstable directions are enslaved: after projecting onto the centre manifold (typically 1–2 dimensional), one can compute normal forms and classify the bifurcation type.
